::: {.hero}
# Jakob Kasper

[Political Psychology · Political Behavior · Affective Polarization]{.lede}
:::

<img src="jakob.jpg" class="headshot" alt="Portrait of Jakob Kasper"/>

I am an incoming **Post-Doctoral Research Fellow** at the [Centre for the Politics of Feelings](https://www.politics-of-feelings.com/), University of London, and am affiliated with the [Hot Politics Lab](https://www.hotpolitics.eu/). I am completing my **PhD** at the University of Amsterdam (Amsterdam School of Communication Research) as part of the MSCA doctoral network [Interdisciplinary Perspectives on the Politics of Adolescence and Democracy](https://www.ippad.eu/) (IP-PAD).

I study **political cognition and behavior**, with a particular focus on **affective polarization**: how to conceptualize and measure it, how it develops from **adolescence** onward, when it becomes a problem for **democracy**, and how to address it when it does. More broadly, I am interested in how **group identities and emotions** shape citizens' political judgments and information sharing, and what consequences this has for the political systems we live in. My work integrates perspectives from psychology and political science, combining measurement validation with large-scale survey experiments and intervention designs.

Before my PhD, I earned a Bachelor's and Master's degree in Psychology at the University of Heidelberg (Germany) and spent a year as a graduate exchange student at Cornell University (USA).
